newsitem.title: UK: S&N concerned by size of Bass estate.
newsitem.headline: S&N concerned by size of Bass estate.

text.p: Scottish & Newcastle Plc expressed concern over the potential size of the public house estate held by rival Bass Plc, if the competition authorities allow a planned merger between Bass and Carlsberg-Tetley to go through unaltered.

Speaking after S&N's annual meeting in Edinburgh, Guy Dickson chairman and managing director of Scottish Courage, S&N's brewing division, called for fairplay from the authorites in dealing with the proposed merger.
"Last year when we took over Courage, S&N was made to cap the number of its pubs to a maximum of 2,675," he said.
"This was but one of several undertakings by ourselves at the time to get the deal through."
Dickson added, "With the Bass situation, it has 4,000 pubs and Allied Domecq ALLD.L a further 4,000. We are concerned over the outcome of such a takeover as to the potential size of estate."
He said, "surely the same rules should apply as regards a capping of public houses when it comes to this planned merger."
Asked if he thought a referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission was likely, Dickson replied "Some people would argue that it should be.
"This is not about sour grapes or market share," he said. "The Office of Fair Trading should look very closely at these proposals, once more details are realised."

The S&N takeover of Courage differed significantly from the proposed Bass deal, "Ours was a north/south deal, with substantial synergies involved, whereas the Bass/Carlsberg proposals involve substantial overlap," Dickson said.
